subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Caffeine Content: Coffee vs. Tea
description: A fast breakdown of Caffeine Content: Coffee vs. Tea for builders.

hook.text: Tea leaves actually contain more caffeine than coffee beans by dry weight. But the cup tells a different story.

buildup.text: A typical cup of coffee has 80–100 mg of caffeine. A cup of black tea has 40–70 mg. Green tea has 20–45 mg.

discovery.text: Coffee uses more grounds per cup and extracts at higher temperatures, pulling out more caffeine per serving.

twist.text: Tea contains L-theanine, an amino acid that smooths caffeine's effect—giving calm alertness instead of jittery energy.

climax.text: Espresso has more caffeine per ounce than any brew—but a small shot has less total caffeine than a full drip coffee.

punchline.text: More caffeine per leaf, less per cup. Brewing makes all the difference.

quiz.question: Why does a cup of coffee have more caffeine than tea?
options: Coffee beans inherently have more caffeine
More grounds and higher water temperature extract more caffeine per cup

details.summary: A standard cup of brewed coffee contains 80 to 100 milligrams of caffeine, while a cup of black tea has 40 to 70 milligrams and green tea 20 to 45 milligrams. These ranges vary widely based on brew time, water temperature, bean variety, and leaf grade.
details.whyItMatters: Knowing approximate caffeine content helps people manage their daily intake and choose beverages that match their sensitivity and energy needs.
takeaways: Brewed coffee averages 80 to 100 mg of caffeine per cup
Black tea contains roughly half the caffeine of coffee
Green tea has the least caffeine among the three

faq.question: Why does the caffeine content of tea vary so much between cups?
faq.answer: Brew time, water temperature, leaf grade, and tea type all affect extraction. A three-minute steep extracts much less caffeine than a five-minute steep, and broken-leaf grades release caffeine faster than whole leaves.

faq.question: Does espresso have more caffeine than regular drip coffee?
faq.answer: Per ounce, espresso has much more caffeine. But a standard espresso shot is only one ounce with about 63 milligrams, while a standard 8-ounce drip coffee has 80 to 100 milligrams total.
